children: Warren Buffett (Trades, Portfolio) said he is stepping down as Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE:BRK.B) chairman, effective immediately. The 96-year-old becomes chairman emeritus and remains a director. His son Howard Buffett takes the chairmanship under a long-standing succession plan, while Susan Decker continues as lead independent director. "Father Time always wins," Buffett wrote. Berkshire Hathaway shares were unchanged.

The move completes a handover already most of the way through. Greg Abel took over as CEO nine months ago with Buffett retaining the chairmanship. Buffett wrote that "Greg runs the company; Howard will guard its culture and values." He said Abel had exceeded his expectations.

Berkshire shares are up 1% in 2026 against more than 11% for the S&P 500, pressured by rising oil prices and a preference for higher-growth names. Investors are waiting to see whether Abel can deploy the $365.5 billion cash pile as Buffett did. He lifted buybacks to $4.5 billion in the second quarter. Over six decades Buffett built a $1 trillion company returning 19.7% a year, nearly double the S&P.

title: Buffett Steps Down as Berkshire Chairman
